title: The Long Colony
premise: Ada Almeida, a xenolinguist who has spent eleven years running cargo and silence along the Long Route, discovers their own name on the manifest of the Meridian, a colony ship that supposedly never flew. The name is a key: the Meridian's crew, frozen in transit for a century, will wake believing Ada is the fleet's appointed arbiter between them and the two rival fleets now converging on the derelict. To keep the lie alive long enough to prevent war, Ada must impersonate a person they never were—while the found family aboard their own ship slowly learns that Ada's lost dreams and missing memories are pieces of the same century-old design. In the end, Ada chooses to become the arbiter truthfully, broadcasting the Meridian's real story to both fleets as the jump window closes, sacrificing their invisibility and their old identity to hold the peace.
about_author: I. M. Oyelaran is a former shipping-log archivist who grew up in three port cities and none of them at once. They write about people who live in the gaps between languages, and this is their second novel.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Ada Almeida, POV. Running routine cargo on the long route, Ada intercepts a fleet registry update listing their name on the Meridian—a colony ship lost before Ada was born. The beat is quiet dread: the life Ada built to be unremarkable just became impossible.

chapters.title: Dreams Without Words
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Flashback-tinged chapter establishing Ada's condition: they stopped dreaming in human languages years ago, speaking instead in something no one recognizes. Crewmate Jun teases; Ada deflects. Beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Kestrel's People
chapters.summary: Jun Okafor, POV. Introduces the small crew of the Kestrel—engineer Sefa, pilot Brannoc, medic Ilse—as a ragged found family who chose each other over fleets. Beat: warmth, and the unspoken rule that no one asks about Ada's past.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Corridor
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Both rival fleets—the Concordance and the Verity Compact—summon every independent hauler for questioning about the Meridian sighting. Ada realizes both sides think the other woke the ship first. Beat: the corridor is closing.

chapters.title: A Name on Ice
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. Sefa helps Ada forge clearance codes to reach the Meridian's public records and finds the crew manifest: one hundred sleepers, and an 'arbiter' designation attached to Ada's name, dated forty years ago. Beat: vertigo—the lie was written before Ada could read.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: Brannoc, POV. Navigation exposition: the only stable jump window to the Meridian opens in twenty-six days and closes fast. Both fleets are racing for it. The Kestrel can beat them both if they leave tonight. Beat: decision under pressure.

chapters.title: What We Don't Ask
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. Ilse privately confronts Ada about their medical history—gaps, implants, the language thing—and offers to come anyway without answers. Beat: found family deepens; trust extended before it's earned.

chapters.title: Departure Without Clearance
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. The Kestrel slips its berth during a Concordance inspection, nearly caught by an officer who seems to recognize Ada's face from somewhere impossible. Beat: exhilaration laced with paranoia.

chapters.title: First Silence
chapters.summary: Jun, POV. Days into the jump corridor, the crew's comms pick up nothing but the Meridian's automated beacon—broadcasting in the same non-human pattern Ada speaks in their sleep. Beat: creeping horror.

chapters.title: The Arbiter's Handbook
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Decrypted Meridian files reveal the arbiter protocol: a linguist trained to hold two hostile parties in negotiation, memory-wiped for neutrality. Ada's condition matches exactly. Beat: identity begins to crack.

chapters.title: Concordance at Our Heels
chapters.summary: Brannoc, POV. A Concordance pursuit ship shadows them through the corridor; Brannoc threads a debris field to lose it, burning fuel they'll need later. Beat: cost of the race made physical.

chapters.title: Verity's Offer
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. A Verity Compact envoy hails the Kestrel with an offer: safe passage and citizenship if they hand over 'the asset.' Ilse refuses without consulting Ada. Beat: loyalty tested by temptation.

chapters.title: Sleep-Talk
chapters.summary: Jun, POV. Jun records Ada talking in their sleep and plays it back: fluent, structured, unmistakably the beacon language. Ada hears themselves and goes cold. Beat: the self becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Arrival: The Meridian
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. The Kestrel docks with the drifting Meridian—dark corridors, frost, a hundred open cryopods, ninety-eight occupied. Two pods are empty. Beat: awe curdling into wrongness.

chapters.title: The Empty Pods
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. Records show two crew woke decades ago: the original arbiter, and a child. Neither logged a return. Sefa finds the arbiter's quarters preserved like a shrine—with Ada's childhood drawing pinned to the wall. Beat: grief for a life Ada can't remember.

chapters.title: Wake Protocol
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. The ship's AI, Meridian-Prime, activates on Ada's voiceprint and addresses them as Arbiter Almeida, briefing them on the negotiation both fleets are coming to force. Ada must decide whether to play the role. Beat: the lie takes its first breath.

chapters.title: Ninety-Eight Strangers
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. Reviving even a few sleepers risks the ships' power balance; Ilse argues for waking the colonists' elected voice, a woman named Captain Reyes. Beat: ethics argued around a med-bay table, family-style.

chapters.title: Reyes Wakes
chapters.summary: Captain Amara Reyes, POV. Reyes wakes a century out of time, learns her colony was used as a bargaining chip between fleets, and meets the 'arbiter' she was told would protect her people. She doesn't believe Ada. Beat: suspicion as mirror.

chapters.title: Both Flags
chapters.summary: Brannoc, POV. First Concordance and Verity ships arrive at the Meridian simultaneously, weapons hot, demanding the arbiter adjudicate claims to the colony. Ada steps onto the comm channel as someone they are not yet. Beat: the performance begins.

chapters.title: The First Lie Holds
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada stalls both fleets with procedural language lifted from the arbiter's handbook, buying days. Privately they begin to suspect the role fits because it was cut to their shape. Beat: competence masking terror.

chapters.title: Jun's Doubt
chapters.summary: Jun, POV. Jun catches Ada practicing Reyes's grandmother's dialect perfectly—a language Ada claims never to have studied. The found family's no-questions rule starts to strain. Beat: love and doubt in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Child Who Left
chapters.summary: Reyes, POV. Ship logs reveal the second empty pod: a girl, woken early, raised aboard a Concordance vessel—the officer who nearly recognized Ada at departure. Beat: the past acquires a face.

chapters.title: Officer Vey
chapters.summary: Officer Nade Vey, POV. Vey boards under truce, sees Ada, and knows her: the arbiter's daughter, presumed dead, the reason the original arbiter abandoned the mission. Vey says nothing—for now. Beat: blackmail hanging unspoken.

chapters.title: Negotiation Table
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Formal talks convene on the Meridian: colony sovereignty versus fleet claims. Ada arbitrates using rules they half-remember dreaming. A near-violent incident is defused by instinct Ada didn't know they had. Beat: the mask becoming muscle.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Says
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. Sefa finally cracks the beacon's full message: not a distress call—an accusation, recorded by the original arbiter, documenting how both fleets' predecessors conspired to strand the colony. Beat: the ground truth changes everything.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Jun, POV. Jun confronts Ada publicly: you knew, or you are, or both. The crew splits—Ilse defends Ada, Brannoc wants to sell the intel and run. Beat: found family breaking along the fault line of identity.

chapters.title: Vey's Price
chapters.summary: Nade Vey, POV. Vey offers Ada a deal: confirm the Concordance's claim and she keeps Ada's origin secret; refuse and she exposes them mid-negotiation, collapsing the talks. Beat: coercion wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Original Arbiter's Log
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada finds the first arbiter's final entry: he left to find his daughter, entrusting his work to the child he'd trained—Ada—wiped and sent out to grow up human. Beat: devastating clarity; the dreams were homework.

chapters.title: Window Closing
chapters.summary: Brannoc, POV. The jump window begins to close; whoever stays past the threshold is committed for a generation. Brannoc puts escape on the table one last time. Beat: the point of no return made literal.

chapters.title: Confession
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada tells the crew everything—the training, the wipe, the name that isn't theirs—and asks them to choose. Ilse stays. Sefa stays. Jun walks to the airlock, then doesn't cycle it. Beat: broken and re-forged family.

chapters.title: Exposure
chapters.summary: Captain Reyes, POV. Vey detonates her secret anyway, revealing to both fleets that the arbiter is a fabricated identity. Talks collapse; weapons arm. Beat: the lie dies loudly.

chapters.title: Mutiny of Small Ships
chapters.summary: Jun, POV. Independent haulers summoned earlier arrive—and side with the Kestrel, refusing to let either fleet take the colony by force. Jun organizes them. Beat: the invisible people choosing visibility together.

chapters.title: Ada's Choice
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Cornered between Vey's guns and the fleets' standoff, Ada realizes the arbiter was never a lie to expose but a function to fulfill. They claim the role openly—not by bloodright, but by consent of everyone present. Beat: identity chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada transmits the original arbiter's accusation, the beacon, and their own testimony in all three languages—human, beacon, and the dream-tongue—to every ship at once. Beat: climax; truth as the only remaining leverage.

chapters.title: Standoff at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Captain Reyes, POV. With the conspiracy public, both fleets' crews waver; rank-and-file sailors refuse the order to fire on a civilian ring. Vey's command fractures. Beat: power failing from the bottom up.

chapters.title: Vey's Fall
chapters.summary: Nade Vey, POV. Offered amnesty within the new accord, Vay must accept the daughter the arbiter chose to save—or the fiction she built her career on. She stands down. Beat: antagonist granted a costly grace.

chapters.title: Signatures
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. The Meridian Accords are signed inside the colony ship itself: the colony sovereign, the route neutral, arbiters drawn from independents. Ada signs a name that is finally theirs by choice. Beat: resolution earned.

chapters.title: Ninety-Eight Neighbors
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. The colonists wake fully into a system that chose to keep them; Ilse treats the last of the thaw cases while the Kestrel's crew becomes the colony's first honored guests. Beat: home where there was none.

chapters.title: Dreaming Again
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. For the first time in years, Ada dreams—in English, in Reyes's dialect, in the beacon tongue, all at once, and wakes weeping and whole. Beat: integration; the divided self made one.

chapters.title: The Long Route, Flown Open
chapters.summary: Jun, POV. The Kestrel departs on the first sanctioned run of the open route, crew intact, carrying mail and news between worlds that speak again. Final image: Ada at the comm, answering a stranger's hail in whatever language they need. Beat: hopeful coda—family, purpose, and a road that stays open.
